name: Palliser shell (1867)
note: Palliser chilled cast iron: the 12" RML's 714 lb shot, W/D³ 0.41. ~1.5% powder ignited by the impact, no fuze. Shatters on any steel face.

name: Common shell, cast iron (1867)
note: Cast iron, ~6% powder, a percussion nose fuze (instant: useless for penetration). W/D³ [EST].

name: Forged steel APC, soft cap (1895)
note: Water-hardened Ni steel under a Makarov soft cap (~+15% below 15°, gone above 20°). W/D³ between Russia's 0.42 and the RN's 0.50 [EST]; filler and the inertial tube's ~0.005 s [EST].

name: Common shell, forged steel (1895)
note: Forged steel common, ~7% powder, base percussion fuze. [EST] from the RN's and Japan's.

name: RU 1895 AP (pyroxylin)
note: 12" AP 'old model' 331.7 kg (W/D³ 0.42), uncapped, 5.3 kg wet pyroxylin, Brink delayed tube (delay [EST]). Light shells did little (Tsushima).

name: RU 1895 HE (pyroxylin)
note: 12" HE 'old model': thin-walled, base-fuzed (the 1894 tube, ~0.005 s), 12.4 kg pyroxylin. A common shell by its fuze.

name: JP 1904 AP (Shimose)
note: 12" 'Furoshiki' 386 kg (W/D³ 0.49), 19.3 kg Shimose, the sensitive Ijuin base fuze: bursts on contact. No 12" known to pierce over ~6".

name: JP 1904 common (powder)
note: 12" common, 39 kg powder (10%): the upper-works fires of Tsushima.

name: US 1906 AP (Explosive D)
note: 12"/45 870 lb (W/D³ 0.50). Explosive D from 1907, the pre-1920s non-delay TNT-boosted base fuze (~0.003 s). Cap and filler share [EST].

name: US 1906 common (powder)
note: Common shell for 1/3-1/2 calibre plate (NOG). Filler [EST].

name: DE 1902 Psgr (TNT)
note: 28 cm/40 240 kg (W/D³ 0.40). TNT from 1902; non-delay before the 1911 Bdz. Cap, filler and fuze [EST].

name: DE 1902 Sprgr Bdz (TNT)
note: Base-fuzed shell. Filler [EST].

name: DE 1902 Sprgr Kz (TNT)
note: Nose-fuzed shell. Filler [EST].

name: FR 1893 AP (powder)
note: Light shells: the 305 Mle 1887's 292 kg (0.37), the 340's 490 kg (0.45). Forged steel, uncapped; filler and fuze [EST].

name: FR 1893 common (Melinite)
note: Melinite (picric acid, catalogued as Lyddite) from 1887. Filler [EST].

name: RN 1906 APC (powder)
note: 12" APC Mk VI 2crh 850 lb (W/D³ 0.49), Hadfield soft cap 73 lb (8.6%), powder-filled (lyddite from 1909-10), No. 16 non-delay. Lord Nelsons kept 2crh.

name: RN 1906 CPC (powder)
note: 12" CPC Mk VIIa: 80 lb powder (9.4%), base fuze.

name: RN 1906 HE (lyddite)
note: 12" HE Mk IIa: 106.5 lb lyddite (12.5%), No. 13 instantaneous nose fuze.

name: RN 1906 light CP (powder)
note: The 4"-6" guns' common pointed (4"/50 31 lb, 6" 100 lb: W/D³ 0.47-0.48). Filler [EST]. Also the RN 1909 and 1912 families' light guns.

name: RN 1906 light HE (lyddite)
note: The 4"-6" guns' lyddite HE. Filler [EST]. Also the RN 1909 and 1912 families' light guns.

name: RN 1909 APC (lyddite)
note: 12" APC Mk VIa 4crh 859 lb (W/D³ 0.50), soft cap 4%, 27.3 lb lyddite, No. 16 non-delay. Breaks up at 15-20° on 0.4 calibre; bursts in the plate (Jutland).

name: RN 1909 CPC (powder)
note: 12" CPC Mk VIIa 4crh: 80 lb powder (9.4%).

name: RN 1909 HE (lyddite)
note: 12" HE: lyddite 12.5%, No. 13 nose fuze (withdrawn from ships after Jutland).

name: RN 1912 APC (lyddite)
note: 15" APC Mk Ia 4crh 1,920 lb (W/D³ 0.57; the 13.5" heavy 1,400 lb the same), 60.5 lb lyddite (3.2%), No. 16 non-delay.

name: RN 1912 CPC (powder)
note: 15" CPC Mk IIa 1,929 lb, 129.3 lb powder (6.7%).

name: RN 1912 HE (lyddite)
note: 15" HE, lyddite. Filler [EST].

name: DE 1911 Psgr L/3,4 (TNT)
note: 30.5 cm Psgr. L/3,4 405 kg (W/D³ 0.52), Krupp Type 2 cap (share [EST]), 10.8 kg TNT, Bdz ~0.025 s nominal: at most half came near it, many duds.

name: DE 1911 Spgr L/3,8 Bdz (TNT)
note: 30.5 cm Spgr. L/3,8 Bdz 405 kg, 24.8 kg TNT: base-fuzed, bursts 2-6 m into unarmoured structure.

name: DE 1911 Spgr Kz (TNT)
note: Nose-fuzed Sprenggranate (the 15 cm's 45.3 kg, 3.0 kg TNT). German light shells ran 0.49-0.54, so the family's blocks serve every gun.

name: FR 1910 OPf (Melinite)
note: 305 Mle 1906 OPf 432 kg (W/D³ 0.55), melinite. Cap, filler and fuze [EST]: French fuzes weren't found.

name: FR 1910 OEA (Melinite)
note: Semi-AP explosive shell. [EST].

name: FR 1910 HE (Melinite)
note: [EST].

name: Standard APC (1912)
note: A middling Great War APC: W/D³ 0.52, soft cap, TNT 2.5%, a short delay. [EST] throughout, from the RN's and Germany's.

name: Standard common (1912)
note: [EST].

name: Standard HE (1912)
note: [EST].

name: US 1916 common (Explosive D)
note: [EST].

name: US 1916 HE (TNT)
note: [EST].

name: US 1916 5in common (Explosive D)

name: US 1916 5in HE (TNT)
note: [EST]. Also the 1921 family's.

name: US 1921 HC (Explosive D)
note: [EST] from the later HC.

name: RN 1927 HE (TNT)

name: RN 1927 light HE (TNT)
note: [EST].

note: [EST].

name: JP 1913 HE (Shimose)
note: [EST].

name: JP 1925 HE (TNT)
note: [EST].

name: JP 1925 light common (TNT/wax)
note: 12.7 cm 23 kg (W/D³ 0.41) and 14 cm 38 kg (0.46). Filler [EST].

name: RU 1911 HE (TNT)
note: 12" HE mod 1911 471 kg, 58.8 kg TNT.

name: RU 1911 light HE (TNT)
note: [EST].

name: RN 1938 HE (TNT)

name: DE 1939 Spgr L/4,5 Kz (TNT)
note: 38 cm nose-fuzed HE 800 kg, 66.2 kg TNT.

name: DE 1939 15cm Spgr Kz (TNT)
note: 15 cm Sprgr. L/4,6 KZ, 3.9 kg TNT.

name: IT 1940 APC (TNT)
note: 381 mm APC 884.8 kg (W/D³ 0.58), cast TNT 10.16 kg (1.15%). Uneven makers: quality 0.95. Cap and fuze [EST].

name: IT 1940 HE (TNT)
